strategy.rule: Final titles, numbers, accusations and thumbnail claims must be re-researched before production. Seeds are angles, not verified assertions.

topics.working_angle: How much does an Amazon delivery driver actually make in the United States, and how does that compare with a professional U.S. truck driver? Explain the difference between Amazon DSP delivery associates and heavy/tractor-trailer truck drivers, compare hourly and annual earnings, show what higher-paid truckers can make, and explain the workload, mileage pay, CDL requirements and time away from home that sit behind the headline numbers.
topics.title_seed: How Much Do Amazon Drivers and U.S. Truckers Really Make?
topics.click_reason: High-curiosity income topic tied to Amazon and one of America's most visible blue-collar careers, with fresh official wage data available in September 2026.
editorial_requirements: Open with the contrast: an Amazon-branded delivery van driver is now near $24 per hour nationally through DSPs, while the median heavy-truck driver earns $58,640 a year.
Explain immediately that most last-mile Amazon delivery drivers in the DSP network are employed by independent Delivery Service Partners, not directly by Amazon.
Use Amazon's September 2026 DSP announcement: national average Delivery Associate earnings are expected to rise to nearly $24 per hour, with pay varying by DSP and geography.

Translate $24 per hour into a simple 40-hour-week annualized illustration of about $49,920 before taxes, clearly label it as an arithmetic illustration rather than guaranteed annual income, and note overtime/hours can change actual earnings.
Use BLS May 2025 wage data for heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers: median $58,640 per year / $28.19 per hour; mean $59,710; lowest 10 percent below $40,140 and highest 10 percent above $79,380.
Explain that heavy truck drivers often are paid by miles driven plus bonuses and normally need a CDL; long-haul drivers can spend days or weeks away from home.

Do not mix company-driver wages with owner-operator gross revenue. If owner-operators are mentioned, make clear revenue is not take-home pay because fuel, insurance, maintenance, truck payments and other costs come out first.
Show realistic monthly and weekly equivalents from verified wage figures, but clearly distinguish calculations from reported wage statistics.
Include why trucking pay varies: route type, experience, region, freight, endorsements, local vs over-the-road, mileage rates, bonuses and overtime.

Keep the documentary angle around the question: is the extra trucking income worth the CDL, hours, safety responsibility and time away from home? Do not answer with a personal recommendation; present the trade-offs factually.

verified_context.claim: Amazon said in September 2026 that new DSP investment is expected to help raise national average Delivery Associate earnings to nearly $24 per hour; exact pay varies by DSP and geography.
Amazon says it has invested $21.7 billion in the DSP program over its eight-year history and announced another $1.9 billion investment for 2027.
The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reports a May 2025 median annual wage of $58,640, or $28.19 per hour, for heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers.
BLS reports that the lowest 10 percent of heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers earned less than $40,140 and the highest 10 percent earned more than $79,380 in May 2025.
BLS reports a May 2025 national mean annual wage of $59,710 for heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers.

reference_media.usage: Reference imagery for Amazon DSP vans, loading, route work and package delivery.
Reference for Amazon delivery van interior and daily-driver workflow.
Primary wage, job requirements and long-haul work-context source for U.S. truck drivers.

topics.working_angle: Meta just unveiled 100-gram VR glasses for $1,299.99. Explain what they are, how the two-part glasses-plus-compute-puck system works, what people can actually do with them, why Meta is making this bet, and put the product in the context of Reality Labs' enormous investment and operating losses without falsely claiming those losses were spent on this single product.
topics.title_seed: Meta's $1,300 VR Glasses Could Replace Your Screens
topics.click_reason: Brand-new Meta Connect 2026 hardware with a concrete $1,299.99 price, unusual 100-gram form factor and a strong business-investment story.
editorial_requirements: Open with the contrast: roughly 100 grams on the face, $1,299.99 price, and one of tech's most expensive long-term VR bets behind it.
Explain clearly that the glasses contain sensors/display while compute, battery and storage live in a tethered external puck.
Cover 5K Infinite Display with micro-OLED, 37 pixels per degree, Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos, Snapdragon Reality Elite, eye/hand/voice input and up to three hours of high-resolution media playback.
Explain use cases: IMAX/3D cinema, 100+ immersive live sports events annually, private multi-screen workspace, flat-surface keyboard/touchpad, gesture gaming/Xbox Cloud Gaming and hologram calling.
State launch window and price: Spring 2027 in the US at $1,299.99.
For development cost, say the exact standalone R&D cost of Meta VR Glasses has not been publicly disclosed.
Use Reality Labs financials only as investment-scale context, not as the development cost of this product.
Include the business strategy: Meta's attempt to own a post-smartphone computing platform and make immersive computing more wearable.
Keep the tone factual, high-curiosity and documentary-style; do not present rumors as confirmed specs.

verified_context.claim: Meta announced Meta VR Glasses on September 23, 2026 and says they weigh about 100 grams, roughly five times lighter than Meta Quest 3.
Meta says the device will go on sale in Spring 2027 for $1,299.99 USD.
Reality Labs recorded a $19.193 billion operating loss in 2025; this is a division-level operating loss and must not be described as the cost of developing these glasses.
Reality Labs recorded an $8.647 billion operating loss in the first six months of 2026; again, this is division-level context, not product R&D cost.

reference_media.usage: Primary factual and visual reference; Meta Newsroom offers downloadable press images.
